title: COWL - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What steps are involved in adjusting the cowl flap controls to ensure full travel and proper closure during rigging?
answer: Rig the Cowl Flap . The cowl flap rigging is typical for each side. Disconnect the cowl flap control devises from the cowl flap shock mounts. Make sure that the flexible controls reach their internal stops in each direction. Identify the controls so that the full travel can be easily examined and maintained while you Set the cowl flap control lever in the CLOSED position. If the control lever cannot be set in the closed position, adjust the controls at the top clevis to position the control lever in the bottom hole of the position bracket. Hold one cowl flap flat with the trailing edge of bottom cowl. Set in position and adjust the clevis to align with the cowl flap mount. Attach the clevis to the shock mount with the bolt, washers and lock nut. Make sure the threads are visible in the clevis inspection holes. Make sure all the clamps and nuts are tight. question: What are the specific steps to detach and reattach the air filter housing when removing and installing the bottom cowl?
answer: Remove the Bottom Cowl . (1) Disconnect the quick-release fasteners from the side cowls and remove the cowls. (2) Loosen the hose clamp installed on the air filter housing hose. (4)  Remove the screws that attach the aft edge of the bottom cowl to the firewall and remove the cowl.Install the Bottom Cowl . title: COWL - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What materials are used for the nose-cap components of the engine?
answer: The engine has a top cowl, two side cowls and a bottom cowl. The front of the engine has a top and bottom or a left and right nose-cap that is made of composite material. The cowls use quick-release fasteners that lock into receptacles for easy removal and installation. The nose-caps attach to each other with screws.There are two cowl flaps in the bottom cowl. They help control the engine temperature and operate by a control lever in the cockpit.

answer: NOTE:  The removal and installation is typical for the left and right side cowl.Remove the Side Cowl . Do not use a regular drill or damage to the receptacle can occur (e) Use a counterbore with an applicable size pilot to fit the pilot hole and spot-face the cowl to 0.470 inch  for the number (1) hole. answer: If Necessary, Install More Fasteners to the Left or Right Side Cowl . NOTE:  As many as two more fasteners can be installed if the cowl does not tightly set on the nose-cap. The illustration shows the left cowl, the right cowl is typical. (1) Make a mark with approximate equal distance between position six and seven, and/or between eight and fourteen for the new fasteners and receptacles. Make sure to keep the same edge distance as the other fasteners. NOTE:  The holes will be drilled with the nose-cap and side cowl attached to make sure the holes are correctly aligned. (2) Remove the side cowl and look to see if there is anything beneath the nose-cap that could be damaged when you drill. Make sure the new recepticle will not touch components beneath the nose-cap such as engine cooling baffles and seals. CAUTION: Make sure before you install the cowl, that you will not drill into anything on the engine side of the nose-cap. (3) Install the side cowl. CAUTION: Use a drill-stop to prevent the drill going to deep and cause damage to something on the engine side of the nose-cap. (4)  Drill with a drill-stop to make a pilot hole in the cowl and nose-cap. (5) Use a counterbore with an applicable size pilot to fit the pilot hole and spot-face the cowl and nose-cap to 0.470 inch . (6) Remove the cowl. (7) Increase the recepticle hole diameter in the nose-cap to 0.562 inch . (8) Install the new fastener in the cowl. (9) Install the new receptacle in the nose-cap.  Remove all metal shavings.  Install the side cowl. Top Cowl Removal/nstallationRemove the Top Cowl . (1) Disconnect the quick-release fasteners from the side cowls and remove the cowls. (2) Remove the screws installed in the aft and forward edges of the top cowl. Keep the screws for the top cowl installation. (3)  Remove the top cowl from the airplane.Install the Top Cowl . (1) Put the top cowl in position on the airplane. (2)  Install the screws in the aft and forward edges of the top cowl. (3) Install the side cowls with the quick-release fasteners.

title: COWL - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How do you properly remove and reinstall the nose-cap on the aircraft during maintenance?
answer: Remove the Nose-Cap . (1) Disconnect the quick-release fasteners from the side cowls and remove the cowls. (2)  Remove the screws that attach the nose-cap to the bottom cowl. Keep the screws for the nose- cap installation. (3)  Remove the screws that attach the two parts of the nose-cap together and remove the two nose- cap pieces.Install the Nose-Cap . (1)  Put the two nose-cap parts in position on the airplane. (2)  Attach the two nose-cap parts together with the screws. (3)  Install the screws that attach the nose-cap to the bottom cowl.

title: COWL - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How do the quick-release fasteners and screws used in the engine cowls and nose-caps improve the process of removing and installing these components?
answer: The engine has a top cowl, two side cowls and a bottom cowl. The front of the engine has a top and bottom or a left and right nose-cap that is made of composite material. The cowls use quick-release fasteners that lock into receptacles for easy removal and installation. The nose-caps attach to each other with screws.There are two cowl flaps in the bottom cowl. They help control the engine temperature and operate by a control lever in the cockpit.

question: What steps should be taken to ensure that a new side cowl is properly fitted, contoured, and aligned with the airplane during installation, including necessary modifications and fastener placement?
answer: NOTE:  The removal and installation is typical for the left and right side cowl.Remove the Side Cowl . (1) Disconnect the quick-release fasteners around the edges of the side cowl and remove the cowl from the airplane.Install the Side Cowl  Install the same cowl you removed. (a) Attach the top edge of the cowl to the airplane. (2) Install a new side cowl. When a new side cowl is installed, it must be fitted to the airplane. The new cowl must be cut and adjusted for the correct fit. The installation for the left and right side of each new side cowl is typical. CAUTION: You must examine the cowl after you complete each step and install each quick-release fastener to make sure the cowl does not wrinkle and the contour of the cowl will match the contour (a) Make sure the cowl matches the contour of the airplane correctly before you install it. The cowl must fit the contour of the airplane without force used to make it fit. Hold the cowl in position on the airplane to examine for the correct contour. If the cowl does not fit the contour of the airplane, it is acceptable to make small form adjustments by hand to help fit the contour. If you cannot form the cowl by hand to the correct contour, then replace the cowl before you try to fit it to the airplane. (b) Set the cowl in position on the airplane with hole number (1) aligned with the receptacle. The holes for the quick-release fasteners are numbered in Figure 202, Detail A. (c) If a new right side cowl is to be installed, material from the cowl must be removed to let the cowl fit on the fuselage edge next to the fuel step handle. CAUTION: Make sure you remove minimal cowl material as necessary. Make a mark for the material to be removed from the cowl for clearance around theRemove the marked material from the cowl. A 0.75 inch  drum sander will work good to remove the cowl (d) Align the cowl on the airplane and use duct tape to hold it in position. Do not use a regular drill or damage to the receptacle can occur (e) Use a counterbore with an applicable size pilot to fit the pilot hole and spot-face the cowl to 0.470 inch  for the number (1) hole. Install a quick-release fastener with a grommet and lock it in position at hole number (1). Remove the duct tape so you can move the cowl as necessary to align the holes that CAUTION: Make sure you spot-face and install the quick-release fasteners and grommets in the sequence shown on Figure 202, Detail A. (h) Use a counterbore to spot-face each pilot hole and install each quick-release fastener and grommet in the sequence shown in Figure 202, Detail A. If the pilot hole is not centered over the receptacle, use a small round file to move the center of the pilot hole so it will be aligned over the receptacle. If you increase the pilot hole diameter in the cowl with a round file, you must change the counterbore pilot to fit the pilot hole. If you do not have the correct size pilot for the counterbore, use a piece of steel sheet-metal and drill a hole to the same diameter as the counterbore pilot which can be used as a template to help guide the counterbore. The template thickness must be sufficient to help keep the counterbore aligned with the receptacle. Use a minimum thickness of 0.032 inch  clearance between the edges of the cowl. If you cut too much off the cowl, the cowl cannot be used. Use an edge scribe to mark a line along all edges of the new cowl, which will give 0.030 to no more than 0.060 inch  clearance between the edges of the cowls. Loosen only the quick-release fasteners as necessary to let the scribe move through that area of the cowl. Make sure you install the quick-release fastener as soon as you move through the area. Remove the cowl and cut just along the outside of the scribed line with sheet metal Smooth the cowl edges with a file and sandpaper to the scribed line. Attach the top edge of the cowl to the airplane. Attach the forward, aft and bottom edges to the airplane. Measure around all edges for the side cowl clearance to make sure there is a 0.030 to 0.060 inch  between the cowls and that there is no overlap of the cowl Disconnect the quick-release fasteners around the new cowl and remove the cowl. (m) Apply the finish paint. Refer to Chapter 12, Airplane Exterior - Cleaning/Painting. Attach the top edge of the cowl to the airplane. Attach the forward, aft and bottom edges to the airplane.
